identity.title: Exploring DCO<SUP>+</SUP> as a tracer of thermal inversion in the disk around the Herbig Ae star HD 163296

paper_type_evidence.quote: This study uses data of DCO$^+$ $J$=3–2 at 216.112 GHz in the disk surrounding the Herbig Ae star HD163296
The data were reduced as described by (cite: Salinas2017) and (cite: Carney2017).

evidence.quote: the Herbig Ae star HD163296 ($\rm\alpha_{2000}$ = ${\rm    17^h56^m51{s}21}$, $\delta_{2000}$ = $-21^\circ57'22{\ensuremath{''}}0$)

question.value: Can a simple 2D chemical model of cold deuteration plus a parametrized warm deuteration channel reproduce the DCO+ J=3-2 emission in the HD 163296 disk, and what do the fitted parameters imply?

evidence.quote: We aim to reproduce the DCO$^+$ emission in the disk around HD163296 using a simple 2D chemical model for the formation of DCO$^+$ through the cold deuteration channel and a parametric treatment of the warm deuteration channel.
as a part of Cycle 2 on 2014 July 27-29 (project 2013.1.01268.S)
obtained by the Atacama Large (sub-)Millimeter Array (ALMA) in Band 6 as a part of Cycle 2

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: DCO+ J=3-2 at 216.112 GHz; spectral resolution 0.7 MHz = 0.085 km/s

evidence.quote: The spectral resolution is 0.7 MHz corresponding to 0.085 km s$^{-1}$ with respect to the rest frequency of the line.
This study uses data of DCO$^+$ $J$=3–2 at 216.112 GHz
The $uv$-coverage of the data ranges from 20 to 630 k$\lambda$.
The resulting synthesized beam has dimensions of 0$\ensuremath{''}$53$\times$0$\ensuremath{''}$42
as a part of Cycle 2 on 2014 July 27-29 (project 2013.1.01268.S)

what.value: Physical structure of the disk (gas density and dust temperature from RADMC) adopted from the parametric model

evidence.quote: We adopt the gas density and dust temperature from the physical model used by (cite: Mathews2013) as inputs for the simple chemical network describe above.

what.value: Simplified analytic DCO+ cold-deuteration chemical network

evidence.quote: This system can be solved analytically as proposed by (cite: Murillo2015). We use their prescription and simplified chemical network of the CD channel and apply it to HD163296.

what.value: Thermal inversion temperature structure motivated by dust evolution models

evidence.quote: A thermal inversion is produced by the dust evolution modeling of (cite: Facchini2017) as a direct consequence of grain growth and settling.
imaged using a Briggs weighting of 0.5
The DCO$^+$ $J$=3–2 line was continuum subtracted in the visibility plane using a first-order polynomial fit and imaged using a Briggs weighting of 0.5.
The resulting synthesized beam has dimensions of 0$\ensuremath{''}$53$\times$0$\ensuremath{''}$42
The data were reduced as described by (cite: Salinas2017) and (cite: Carney2017).

what.value: Keplerian mask for integrated intensity and residual radial profiles

evidence.quote: The residual radial profile is obtained applying a Keplerian mask (cite: Salinas2017) to the residual cube

what.value: Column density prescription and excitation temperature profile

evidence.quote: This 1D analysis was previously performed by (cite: Salinas2017) and we use the same prescription and excitation temperature profile for DCO$^+$.

analysis_steps.goal: Build radial emission profile from the data

method.value: Keplerian mask to make integrated intensity map; average over concentric ellipses centered on the star

evidence.quote: A radial emission profile can be constructed by taking the average value of concentric ellipsoids, centered at the star, in the integrated intensity map.

analysis_steps.goal: Compute DCO+ abundance with simplified cold-deuteration network

method.value: Analytic 10-reaction network of Murillo+2015 on adopted Mathews+2013 density and temperature structure

evidence.quote: The DCO$^+$ chemical network involving the CD channel can be boiled down to only ten chemical reactions.
The ionization rate ($\zeta$) is constant throughout the disk and equal to$1.3\times10^{-17}$ s$^{-1}$.

key_parameters.value: Standard model X_high=5e-5, T_CO=19 K, radial cutoff 300 AU

evidence.quote: We chose a standard CO abundance model with a constant abundance $X_{\rm high}$=5.0$\times10^{-5}$ at temperatures above an evaporation temperature of $T_{\rm CO}$=19 K.

assumptions.value: T_dust = T_gas; HD abundance equals the cosmic D/H ~1e-5; X_low = 0.01 X_high

evidence.quote: We assume that the dust temperature ($T_{\rm dust}$) equals the gas temperature ($T_{\rm gas}$), which is a reasonable assumption in the dense regions that we focus on.

fitting.value: Parameters adjusted to match the observed profile; no sampler stated

evidence.quote: These values are taken to match the inner DCO$^+$ emission at R$\lesssim$ 150 AU.

validation.value: Network compared with full chemical models by Murillo+2015

evidence.quote: They contrasted their results to a full chemical network including gas-grain balance (freeze-out, thermal desorption, and cosmic-ray-induced photodesorption) confirming the general trend found by the simplified network.

analysis_steps.goal: Non-LTE radiative transfer and comparison with data

method.value: LIME model cube, continuum subtracted with first channel, convolved with the synthesized beam, compared with data radial profile

evidence.quote: Then, each spectral plane of the model is convolved with the synthesized beam of the DCO$^+$ data cube.
We use a grid of 100000 points that are created applying a weighted random selection in $R$ using a logarithmic scale.

validation.value: Convergence checked by comparing consecutive iterations

evidence.quote: We manually set the number of iterations to 20 and confirm convergence by comparing consecutive iterations.

analysis_steps.goal: Residual abundance estimate for WD contribution

method.value: Subtract convolved model cube from data channel by channel, Keplerian mask, radial profile, LTE optically thin column density divided by surface density

evidence.quote: We perform a channel by channel subtraction from the data cube and the convolved model cube to calculate a residual cube
The radial abundance estimate is calculated assuming LTE and that the emission is optically thin.

analysis_steps.goal: Add thermal inversion (CD+TI) and warm deuteration (CD+WD+TI)

method.value: Temperature increased by parametrized term with R1=240 AU, R2=300 AU; X_WD added where T<=T_eff

evidence.quote: where $R_1=240$ AU is the inflection point at which the TI occurs and $R_2=300$ AU a characteristic radius.

key_parameters.value: X_high=2.0e-7, T_CO=19 K; X_WD=3.2e-12, T_eff=32 K

evidence.quote: using $X_{\rm WD}=3.2\times10^{-12}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$= 32 K and the parameters from the CD+TI model

fitting.value: Values chosen to match the observed profile

evidence.quote: These values are taken to match the inner DCO$^+$ emission at R$\lesssim$ 150 AU.

used_for.value: 3D non-LTE radiative transfer of DCO+ model

evidence.quote: We used LIME (v1.5), a 3D radiative transfer code in non-LTE (cite: Brinch2010)

used_for.value: dust temperature profile of the adopted physical model

evidence.quote: The dust temperature profile was computed by the 2D radiative transfer code RADMC (cite: Dullemond2004b)
cold deuteration producing abundances up to $1.6\times 10^{-11}$
Warm deuteration, at a constant abundance of $3.2\times 10^{-12}$
becomes fully effective below 32 K
a CO abundance of $2\times 10^{-7}$ is found

results_numeric.quantity: WD/CD DCO+ ratio outside CO snowline

evidence.loc: 4.2 Low vs high temperature deuteration pathways
evidence.quote: ratio between the DCO$^+$ column densities produced by the WD and the CD channel of  0.2
attributed to a temperature inversion at 250 AU

findings_qualitative.value: Thermal inversion or increased photodesorption can explain the DCO+ outer bump and cutoff; the models cannot distinguish them.

evidence.quote: Our modeling cannot distinguish this from thermal desorption.

claims.hypothesis: Simple CD chemistry with a temperature inversion reproduces the outer DCO+ morphology
claims.experiment: CD+TI model in LIME compared with the observed radial profile
claims.result: Reproduces shape at R>180 AU and the lack of emission at R>300 AU with X_high=2e-7
claims.finding: A thermal inversion near 250 AU can cause the secondary maximum and limit DCO+ extent

evidence.quote: can reproduce the radial shape of the DCO$^+$ in the disk around HD163296 at $R>180$ AU and the lack of emission at $R>300$ AU.

claims.hypothesis: The WD channel contributes to inner DCO+ emission
claims.experiment: Add constant X_WD below T_eff to CD+TI
claims.finding: WD contributes up to ~20%, consistent with Favre et al. models

evidence.quote: The ratio of the amount of DCO$^+$ produced by the WD and CD channels outside the CO snowline in this model is 0.2, consistent with previous full chemical models of DCO$^+$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Drop in gas density, higher o/p H2, and higher electron fraction judged unlikely for the DCO+ outer drop

evidence.quote: It is therefore unlikely that the drop off of DCO$^+$ is due to an overall drop in gas surface density.

limitations_admitted.value: T_eff cannot be constrained without a gas temperature model, and photodesorption cannot be distinguished from thermal desorption

evidence.quote: The exact value of the parameter $T_{\rm eff}$ cannot be constrained without a gas temperature model and only represents the location of the isothermal surface.

referee_caveats_inferred: Parameters tuned by eye without uncertainties or formal fit
Degeneracy between CO abundance and T_CO
Gas temperature assumed equal to dust temperature
Thermal inversion parametrization is ad hoc
